<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />{{GHGmargin-letter|134|s}}
Rem. The collocation of a numeral with the next above it (either in the same or in different sentences) is a rhetorical device employed in ''numerical sayings'' to express a number, which need not, or cannot, be more exactly specified. It must be gathered from the context whether such formulae are intended to denote only an insignificant number (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}, ''two or'' at the most ''three''), or a considerable number, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}. Sometimes, however, this juxtaposition serves to express merely an indefinite total, without the collateral idea of intensifying the lower by means of the higher number. Thus ''one'' and ''two'' are connected by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=12}}); ''two'' and ''three'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=23|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=26|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=50|verse=25|hidebook=1}}), and without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=8}}; ''three'' and ''four'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=1|verse=3}}–11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=29|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=26|verse=5}}), and without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=15}}; ''four'' and ''five'', without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=6}}; ''six'' and ''seven'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=16}}; ''seven'' and ''eight'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=11|verse=2}}; (''nine'' and ''ten'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Sirac|chapter=25|verse=7}}).<section end=par134 />

<section begin=par135 />{{center|III. Syntax of the Pronoun.}}

<!-- section begins above -->{{GHGpar-heading|135|The Personal Pronoun}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|a}}
'''1.''' The ''separate'' pronouns,—apart from their employment as the subject in noun-clauses (cf. {{GHGpar|141|a}}) and the idiom mentioned under ''d–h'',—are used, according to {{GHGpar|32|b}}, as a rule, only to give express emphasis to the subject; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}} i.e. ''I myself'', so also {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=15|hidebook=1}} (after the verb), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=6}};<ref>Also {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִיא|translate=he himself, she herself}} (of persons and things), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי הוּא|translate=the Lord himself}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַיְּהוּדִים הֵ֫מָּה|translate=the Jews themselves}}. In the sense of ''the same'' (ὁ αὐτός) or (''one and'') ''the same'', {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} is used in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, 13, 46:4, 48:12 (always {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי הוּא}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=28}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה הוּא}}), and probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=19}}.—The position of {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}, as an accusative of the object, before a perfect in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=9|verse=22}}, can at most be explained on the analogy of Aramaic ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=5|verse=12}}).</ref> but {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי|translate=I}} and none else; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי אֲנִי|translate=I, I!}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=14}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=56}} (as in 20:8, 22:18, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=21}}, after the imperative); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=19}} (after the verb, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=12}}); fem. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=5}}.—Sometimes, however, the separate pronoun appears to be placed before the verb more on rhythmical grounds, i.e. in order to give the statement a fuller sound than that of the bare verbal form (cf. the similar use of the infinitive absolute, {{GHGpar|113|o}}). Thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=2}}, and most clearly in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=30|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=21|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=18}} (in solemn promises). The same explanation applies to {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} at the beginning of sentences, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=45}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=5|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=82|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=3}}.<ref>As early as the Mêšaʿ inscription (line 21 ff.) {{GHGheb|text=אנך}} frequently stands at the beginning of a new sentence after the dividing stroke.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|b}}
Rem. 1. Different from this is the pleonastic addition of the separate pronoun immediately ''after'' the verb (according to Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=5}} perhaps<section end=par135 /><noinclude>
